kept.title: Incorrect handling of --save-exact without --save or --save-dev in install function
kept.explanation: The condition to apply --save-exact only when --save or --save-dev is present was removed, allowing --save-exact alone to modify the _json object in memory but never actually save the dependencies or devDependencies to bower.json. This results in unexpected behavior where the --save-exact flag alone does not persist versions to bower.json, and users might incorrectly expect dependencies to be saved.
kept.suggestion: Restore the conditional to require --save or --save-dev for modifying dependencies or devDependencies, or update logic to handle saving dependencies properly when only --save-exact is used.
kept.failureAfterChange: Running `bower install <package>` with only --save-exact flag (no --save or --save-dev) does not write any dependencies to bower.json, although the versions appear set in memory.

verdicts.reason: The finding accurately points out that the code change removed the condition that prevented --save-exact from modifying the in-memory dependencies unless --save or --save-dev was specified. This leads to a behavior where the dependencies are set in memory but are never actually saved to the bower.json file, which is a concrete defect introduced by the current code change. Thus, the finding describes a real issue existing after this change.
